title: Restricted-direction incidence graphs for the C4 C6 and C10 lower bounds
difficulty_reason: The author chooses the moment-curve directions (1,t,...,t^(k-1)) to produce q^k lines on q^k points and q^(k+1) incidences. The essential new verification converts a putative 2k-cycle into a zero sum of direction vectors with nonzero coefficients. Vandermonde independence forces every direction to repeat, while consecutive intersecting distinct lines cannot be parallel; these requirements are incompatible for k=2,3,5. This coordinated choice of direction set, cycle translation and repetition obstruction supplies a non-routine construction and proof. The Vandermonde determinant and finite-field linear algebra remain ordinary prerequisites, not counted new material. The prime rounding/edge count alone is H1; the complete selected theorem includes its construction and full freeness core as author proof, one unit.

core_obligations: Choose the restricted finite-field line directions so that the incidence edge count has the target exponent.
Translate the whole cycle to a vanishing nonzero-coefficient sum and enforce Vandermonde independence/repeated directions.
Use cyclic adjacency and k in {2,3,5} to rule out the resulting repetition pattern.
historical_route_credit: Existence due to Benson (1966), Singleton (1966); construction due to Wenger (1991), simplified description Conlon (2021), printed Remark1.10.16; book exposition Yufei Zhao.
internal_overlap: The k=2 specialization overlaps the weaker C4 exponent of1.10.1; no extra item is claimed for k=2,3,5 separately. The k=3,5 construction/freeness is not implied by the polarity result, so the full family gives one additional unit.
